🧳 External / portable drive · 🪫 Won't power on / dead

External Hard Drive Not Spinning or Won't Power On

If an external drive has no lights or sound, the cause may be a bad cable, a dead power adapter, a failed bridge board (the small board that turns USB into the drive's own connection) or a failed drive. A burnt smell points to an electrical fault, so stop trying.

4/5 · High risk
Success odds: Low

Cable and adapter checks are safe, but repeated attempts on a drive with an electrical or motor fault can make things worse.

✋ Stop! Don't do this first

  • Unplug it if you smell burning or see scorch marks. Do not power it up again.
  • Do not keep switching it on and off hoping it starts.
  • Do not use the freezer trick, and never open the drive. It needs a cleanroom.
  • Do not use a power adapter that is not the one it came with. The wrong voltage can burn the board.

Your steps

0 of 7 done
  1. Show me how
    1. Unplug everything. Look at the USB port on the drive for bent, loose or broken pins.
    2. Sniff for a burnt smell. Loose or broken ports are common on portables.
  2. Show me how
    1. Try one other USB cable and port, then one other computer.
    2. For desktop-style drives, check the wall adapter is the original one and test the outlet with a lamp.
  3. Show me how
    1. Plug it in and watch for an LED light on the drive. Rest a fingertip on it for 10 seconds.
    2. Lights but no hum: suspect the drive or motor. No lights: suspect cable, power or bridge board.
    3. Switch off after one try.
  4. Show me how
    1. Do not try swapping the bridge board or putting the drive in another case.
    2. Search your exact model number plus 'encryption' to see if it uses hardware encryption.
  5. Show me how
    1. Do not pry the drive out unless you know it has a normal SATA connector and is not hardware encrypted.
    2. If unsure, leave the case closed and ask a recovery professional.

    Guide: How to find a trustworthy data recovery professional

  6. Show me how
    1. Follow our imaging guide with ddrescue onto a different drive. Always type the failing drive first and the empty destination second. If you swap them, the copy erases your data.
    2. Then run TestDisk or PhotoRec on the image file.

    Guide: How to make an image (exact copy) of a driveGuide: How to use TestDisk to copy files off a driveGuide: How to use PhotoRec to recover photos and files

  7. Show me how
    1. Unplug it and pack it in a padded box.
    2. Tell the lab what you saw, heard and smelled.

    Guide: How to find a trustworthy data recovery professional

Mission complete! 🎉 Check your recovered files open properly, then back them up in two places.

Tools you'll use

GNU ddrescue

Copies a failing drive to an image file, retrying bad areas so you work from a copy, not the original.

  • Linux · macOS
  • Free (open source)

smartmontools

Free open-source suite that reads S.M.A.R.T. health data from drives to show early signs of failure.

Questions people ask

No lights at all. Is the drive dead?

Not necessarily. A broken cable, adapter, USB port or bridge board can look the same. Try other cables and computers before giving up.

Can I take the drive out and connect it directly?

Only if it has a standard SATA connector and is not encrypted by the case. Many portables do not, so check the exact model first.

Is a loose USB port fixable?

It can be, but soldering takes skill, and a poor repair can damage the board. Ask an expert for valuable data.
